name: Crucible Fab-Floor Welder's Full Shift Kit
description:
A full shift kit for arc-welding and fabrication floor work at a Crucible manufacturing facility. The outer layer is a flame-retardant coverall in deep charcoal synth-canvas with Crucible's angular red-and-black logo heat-pressed onto the left chest and upper back. The coverall is cut generously through the shoulders and arms to accommodate chrome arm augmentation — the sleeves feature a double-snap expansion gusset at the forearm that opens wide enough to slide over a full prosthetic limb, then closes flush against the wrist seal. The collar is high and reinforced, with an auto-sealing zip that locks against flash exposure. Welding burn marks — small, circular, orange-edged — dot the forearms and thighs, a badge of regular use rather than negligence.

Underneath: a Crucible-issued moisture-wicking thermal shirt in dark gray with a banded collar. The boots are Penrose Weld Boots — broad-toed, ankle-high, with metatarsal guards and a magnetic sole-strip for standing on metal grating. A welding helmet — Crucible-branded, auto-darkening visor, worn pushed up on the forehead between tasks — completes the headwear. Heavy-duty welding gauntlets in tan leather-analog with cuff extensions are tucked under one arm. A fabric tool-loop apron in heavy cotton duck ties at the waist over the coverall, holding wire brushes, a chipping hammer, and a seam gauge. The whole kit smells of flux and hot metal.
functionality: Flame-retardant outer layer, chrome-arm expansion gussets on sleeves, auto-sealing collar zip, metatarsal-guard boots with magnetic sole-strip, auto-darkening welding helmet, tool-loop apron, moisture-wicking base layer
what_it_says: A Crucible floor worker — experienced enough to have earned the burn marks, careful enough that none of them are serious. The chrome-arm gussets are a tell: this person has at least one prosthetic limb, probably a workplace injury claim that Crucible settled with a company-plan replacement rather than Quanta. They do the dangerous work that makes the city's infrastructure. They are not asking for your sympathy.
price_range: Φ 210–Φ 290 (corponation-issued kit; boots and apron worker-purchased)
story_hooks: The chrome-arm gusset on a welder's coverall has been modified to smuggle small fabricated components out of the facility past mag-strip scanners — someone on the inside is building something piece by piece.

A Crucible floor worker is the only witness to a fatal 'accident' on the fab floor, and their continued employment — and the company-plan chrome arm they can't afford to replace privately — depends on their silence.
The tool apron contains a hand-drawn map stitched into the lining, detailing a section of Crucible's sub-basement that doesn't appear on any official schematic.
related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian full-body work kit designed for industrial arc-welding. The silhouette is deliberately loose and accommodating through the shoulders and arms, tapering slightly at the waist where a tool apron cinches it. The coverall dominates the visual presentation — a heavy, functional garment that reads as serious labor. The welder's helmet perched on the forehead adds an iconic industrial edge. Overall impression: a seasoned factory floor worker, augmentation-ready, marked by honest wear.
physical_description.fit: Generously cut through shoulders, chest, and arms to accommodate chrome prosthetic limbs. Standard straight leg through hips and thighs. Wrist seals are precision-fitted. The tool apron sits snug at the waist over the coverall. Boots are broad and grounded.
physical_description.primary_material: Outer: flame-retardant synth-canvas (charcoal). Undershirt: moisture-wicking thermal blend (dark gray). Boots: ballistic rubber with metal-mesh metatarsal guards. Gauntlets: tan leather-analog with cuff extensions. Tool apron: heavy cotton duck. Helmet: polycarbonate visor with auto-darkening lens.
physical_description.texture: Canvas is slightly rough and textured, broken-in to a soft nap in high-wear areas. Thermal undershirt is smooth and slightly stretchy. Leather-analog gauntlets are supple but reinforced. Boots have a weathered grip texture on soles. Burn marks create subtle raised, slightly charred circular textures across forearms and thighs.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep charcoal synth-canvas as primary. Dark gray thermal undershirt. Tan leather-analog gauntlets. Black rubber boots. Accent colors: Crucible's angular red-and-black logo heat-pressed on chest and upper back. Orange-edged welding burn marks scattered across forearms and thighs. Brass-colored tool handles peek from apron pockets.
physical_description.closures: Auto-sealing high-collar zip on coverall (locked against flash exposure). Double-snap expansion gussets at both forearms (opens wide for prosthetic insertion, closes flush at wrist seal). Tool apron ties at waist with heavy-duty cord. Gauntlets pull on, held in place by friction and wrist seals.
distinctive_features: Double-snap forearm gussets designed for chrome limb accommodation
Heat-pressed Crucible corporate logo (angular red-and-black) on left chest and upper back
Auto-sealing high-collar zip for flash protection
Authentic welding burn marks: small, circular, orange-edged, scattered across forearms and thighs
Weld helmet with auto-darkening visor, worn pushed up on forehead
Magnetic sole-strip on Penrose boots for metal grating adhesion
Tool-loop apron with wire brushes, chipping hammer, and seam gauge
Heavy-duty tan leather-analog gauntlets with cuff extensions
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4: Working class, heavy industrial labor. The kit is high-function but not luxury — Crucible-issued standard equipment. The wear patterns and authentic burn marks signal someone who actually uses this gear daily, not a costume.
physical_description.cultural_context: Factory floor worker, manufacturing sector, Crucible facility employee. The augmentation-ready design (especially the forearm gussets) signals either current chrome limb ownership or anticipated future augmentation — common in manufacturing hubs. Wearing this marks you as essential infrastructure labor, competent and experienced.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-worn and broken-in. The canvas shows soft creasing at joints. Burn marks are genuine and numerous — not fresh, but not ancient. The tool apron is actively used. Gauntlets show leather-analog creasing and grip marks. Boots are scuffed but maintained. The whole kit has the comfortable, capable patina of daily use by someone who knows their equipment.
